words.enDefinition: A running instance of a program together with its execution state and resources.

examples.en: The task viewer showed a separate process when we opened another copy of the drawing app.
examples.zh: 我们又打开一份绘图应用时，任务查看器显示了一个单独的「进程」。

examples.en: Our example used one process for the editor and another for the image conversion tool.
examples.zh: 例题为编辑器使用一个「进程」，并给图像转换工具使用另一个。

words.enDefinition: A number the operating system uses to identify a particular active process.

examples.en: The monitor displayed a process identifier next to each copy of the sample text editor.
examples.zh: 监视器在示例文本编辑器的每个实例旁显示了「进程标识符」。

examples.en: We matched the process identifier from the log with the one shown in the task viewer.
examples.zh: 我们把日志中的「进程标识符」与任务查看器显示的标识对应起来。

words.enDefinition: A process that creates another process.

examples.en: The parent process started a second program to convert the photographs used in our classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 「父进程」启动了另一个程序，转换课堂练习中使用的照片。

examples.en: We checked whether the parent process waited for both image conversions before showing the summary.
examples.zh: 我们核查「父进程」是否等两项图像转换完成后才显示摘要。

collocations: the parent process starts a child

words.enDefinition: A process created by another process.

examples.en: The classroom launcher started a child process to count the words in the sample document.
examples.zh: 课堂示例的启动器启动了一个「子进程」，统计示例文档中的词数。

examples.en: We let the child process finish its conversion before displaying the new thumbnail in the example.
examples.zh: 例题中，我们等「子进程」完成转换后才显示新缩略图。

words.enDefinition: The operating system's work of setting up a new process and its resources.

examples.en: The lab traced process creation when the sample launcher opened a helper for each image.
examples.zh: 当示例启动器给每张图片打开一个辅助程序时，实验跟踪了「进程创建」。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why process creation involved setting up more than a new program counter.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么「进程创建」涉及的工作多于设置一个新的程序计数器。

collocations: measure the cost of process creation
observe process creation in a task viewer

words.enDefinition: The end of a process's execution, when the operating system can release associated resources.

examples.en: The trace recorded process termination after the preview helper had finished all three requested conversions.
examples.zh: 预览辅助程序完成所要求的三项转换后，跟踪记录记下了「进程终止」。

examples.en: We checked the time of process termination before comparing the two recordings of the classroom demonstration.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「进程终止」时间，再比较课堂演示的两份记录。

words.enDefinition: a classification of a process in an operating system or teaching model, such as ready, running, waiting or terminated

examples.en: The simulator showed the process state changing when the image program began waiting for a file.
examples.zh: 图像程序开始等待文件时，模拟器显示「进程状态」发生变化。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked which process state applied after the task finished waiting for input.
examples.zh: 练习表问，任务结束对输入的等待后会进入哪种「进程状态」。

words.enDefinition: An operating system structure holding records about processes it is managing.

examples.en: The diagram showed a process table with a record for each job in the exercise.
examples.zh: 图中展示了一个「进程表」，练习中的每项作业各有一条记录。

examples.en: We located the editor's entry in the process table before checking the recorded process state.
examples.zh: 我们先在「进程表」找到编辑器的记录，再核查记载的进程状态。

collocations: look up a process in the process table
store an entry in the process table

words.enDefinition: A kernel record that stores management information and execution state for a process.

examples.en: The tutor drew a process control block next to each process in the scheduling example.
examples.zh: 老师在调度例题的每个进程旁画了一个「进程控制块」。

examples.en: We used the process control block to explain how the simulator remembered where a process stopped.
examples.zh: 我们用「进程控制块」解释模拟器怎样记住进程上次停在何处。

collocations: save state in a process control block

words.enDefinition: The program code, data, and other memory contents associated with a process's current execution.

examples.en: The diagram showed code and data in different regions of the same process image.
examples.zh: 图中显示，代码和数据位于同一个「进程映像」的不同区域。

examples.en: Our tutor used a process image to explain what memory the program had while it ran.
examples.zh: 老师用「进程映像」说明程序运行时有哪些内存区域。

collocations: inspect the layout of a process image

words.enDefinition: In a shell, a process in the foreground job that can interact with the terminal.

examples.en: The shell waited for the foreground process to finish displaying its results before accepting another command.
examples.zh: Shell 等「前台进程」显示完结果后才接受另一条命令。

examples.en: In our terminal exercise, the foreground process handled the input we typed during the demonstration.
examples.zh: 终端练习中，「前台进程」处理了演示期间我们键入的内容。

collocations: show output from a foreground process

words.enDefinition: A process running without taking over the user's current foreground interaction.

examples.en: The example image converter ran as a background process while we continued working in the editor.
examples.zh: 示例图像转换器作为「后台进程」运行，我们则继续在编辑器里工作。

examples.en: Our tutor checked whether the background process had finished before opening the converted images.
examples.zh: 老师先查「后台进程」是否完成，再打开转换后的图片。

words.enDefinition: Work whose completion time is mainly limited by CPU computation.

examples.en: The example image filter was a CPU-bound workload once all the pixels were already in memory.
examples.zh: 所有像素都已在内存中时，示例图像滤镜的运算是「计算受限的工作负载」。

examples.en: We plotted CPU use for a CPU-bound workload that repeatedly resized a set of sample images.
examples.zh: 我们为反复调整一组样图尺寸的「计算受限的工作负载」绘出了 CPU 使用率。

collocations: compare a CPU-bound workload with an I/O-bound one

words.enDefinition: Work whose completion time is mainly limited by waiting for input or output operations.

examples.en: The copy job was an I/O-bound workload because it spent most of its time awaiting storage.
examples.zh: 复制任务大部分时间都在等存储设备，因此属于「I/O 受限的工作负载」。

examples.en: Our worksheet compared an I/O-bound workload reading large files with a calculation done entirely in memory.
examples.zh: 练习表对比了读取大文件的「I/O 受限的工作负载」和完全在内存中进行的运算。

collocations: measure waiting in an I/O-bound workload

words.enDefinition: A sequence of instructions that can be scheduled independently within a process.

examples.en: Each thread of execution had a separate position in the code shown in the diagram.
examples.zh: 在图示代码中，每个「执行线程」都有自己独立的执行位置。

examples.en: The sample app used a separate thread of execution to prepare a preview while editing continued.
examples.zh: 示例应用使用另一个「执行线程」准备预览，让编辑工作可以继续。

words.enDefinition: A value that distinguishes a thread within the scope defined by its operating system or runtime.

examples.en: The program printed a thread identifier beside each completed photo conversion in the example log.
examples.zh: 程序在示例日志中每项已完成的照片转换旁打印了「线程标识符」。

examples.en: We used the thread identifier to tell which worker had produced each line in the report.
examples.zh: 我们用「线程标识符」判断是哪个工作线程生成了报告中的各行。

collocations: match output to a thread identifier

words.enDefinition: The initial thread of execution in an application or process.

examples.en: The sample kept the main thread available to respond while another thread prepared the preview.
examples.zh: 示例让另一个线程准备预览，这样「主线程」可以继续响应。

examples.en: We waited for the main thread to print the summary after both workers finished their calculations.
examples.zh: 两条工作线程都完成计算后，我们等「主线程」打印摘要。

words.enDefinition: A thread assigned work on behalf of another part of a program.

examples.en: A worker thread prepared the miniature images while the practice editor continued accepting new input.
examples.zh: 「工作线程」在准备缩略图，练习编辑器可以继续接收新的输入。

examples.en: We checked which worker thread had processed the last batch of sample photographs that afternoon.
examples.zh: 我们查了当天下午是哪条「工作线程」处理完最后一批示例照片。

collocations: assign a task to a worker thread

words.enDefinition: A group of threads managed together to take on tasks, usually with workers reused between tasks.

examples.en: The thread pool reused the same workers to resize several batches of sample photographs.
examples.zh: 「线程池」重复使用同一批工作线程来调整几批示例照片的大小。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how one thread pool handled jobs from two different parts of the application.
examples.zh: 老师展示了一个「线程池」怎样处理应用中两个不同部分提交的作业。

collocations: submit a task to a thread pool

words.enDefinition: To wait until another thread finishes execution.

examples.en: The exercise asked us to join a thread before reading the total that it had calculated.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们先「等待线程结束」，再读取它算出的总数。

examples.en: We needed to join a thread before closing the sample window that displayed its work.
examples.zh: 在关闭显示工作结果的示例窗口前，我们需要先「等待线程结束」。

collocations: join a thread before using its result
join a thread after starting it
decide where to join a thread

words.enDefinition: Storage giving each thread its own instance of a variable or value.

examples.en: The example used thread-local storage to keep each worker's temporary counter separate from the others.
examples.zh: 例题使用「线程局部存储」为各条工作线程分别保存临时计数器。

examples.en: Our tutor showed why one worker's update to thread-local storage did not change another worker's value.
examples.zh: 老师演示了为什么某条工作线程更新「线程局部存储」后，另一条线程的值不会改变。

collocations: read a value from thread-local storage
store a counter in thread-local storage

words.enDefinition: An operating system component that selects runnable work for a CPU to execute.

examples.en: The process scheduler gave another task time to run while the first waited for input.
examples.zh: 第一项任务等待输入时，「进程调度器」让另一项任务占用 CPU 运行。

examples.en: Our simulator recorded which task the process scheduler selected each time a processor became available.
examples.zh: 每次处理器空闲时，模拟器都记录「进程调度器」选中了哪项任务。

collocations: decisions made by the process scheduler

words.enDefinition: A task eligible to use a CPU because it is not blocked on an event.

examples.en: The simulator marked the print job as a runnable task after its input had arrived.
examples.zh: 输入到达后，模拟器把打印作业标为「可运行任务」。

examples.en: We checked why the runnable task still had to wait even though its data was available.
examples.zh: 即使数据已经就绪，我们还检查了为什么这项「可运行任务」仍需等待。

collocations: place a runnable task in the ready queue

words.enDefinition: A scheduler's collection of tasks eligible to run but waiting for CPU time.

examples.en: The ready queue contained three tasks waiting for time on the single simulated processor.
examples.zh: 「就绪队列」里有三项任务，都在等待同一个模拟处理器分配时间。

examples.en: We watched one job leave the ready queue when the simulator selected it to run.
examples.zh: 模拟器选中一项作业运行时，我们看到它离开了「就绪队列」。

collocations: add a task to the ready queue
select a task from the ready queue

words.enDefinition: in a scheduling model distinguishing ready from running, the state of a task currently executing on a processor

examples.en: The diagram used a green box for the process in the running state on that core.
examples.zh: 图中用绿色方框标示在该核心上处于「运行状态」的进程。

examples.en: Our simulator marked a task as being in the running state when it was executing instructions.
examples.zh: 任务正在执行指令时，模拟器将它标为「运行状态」。

collocations: mark a task as being in the running state

words.enDefinition: The state of a task that cannot continue until a required event occurs.

examples.en: The task entered a blocked state while it waited for the simulated storage device to respond.
examples.zh: 任务等待模拟存储设备响应期间进入「阻塞状态」。

examples.en: We watched the task leave the blocked state after the worksheet indicated that input had arrived.
examples.zh: 练习表显示输入已到达后，我们看到任务退出了「阻塞状态」。

words.enDefinition: Saving the execution state of one task and restoring that of another so it can run.

examples.en: The trace recorded a context switch when the scheduler replaced the running task with another one.
examples.zh: 调度器用另一项任务替换当前运行的任务时，跟踪记录显示发生了「上下文切换」。

examples.en: We drew a context switch between two tasks to show which registers needed to be saved.
examples.zh: 我们画出了两项任务之间的「上下文切换」，以展示需要保存哪些寄存器。

collocations: measure the overhead of a context switch

words.enDefinition: The limited interval during which a scheduler allows a task to run before reconsidering its choice.

examples.en: Each simulated task got a time slice before the next eligible task could take its turn.
examples.zh: 下一项符合条件的任务轮到之前，每项模拟任务都有一个「时间片」。

examples.en: Our worksheet changed the time slice to show how often the simulator switched between the two tasks.
examples.zh: 练习表改变「时间片」的长度，展示模拟器在两项任务之间的切换频率。

collocations: choose the length of a time slice

words.enDefinition: Scheduling in which the scheduler may pause a running task to let a different task run.

examples.en: With preemptive scheduling, the simulator could pause a long calculation and let a second task run.
examples.zh: 在「抢占式调度」下，模拟器可以暂停一段长运算，让第二项任务运行。

examples.en: Our tutor used a timeline to show when preemptive scheduling interrupted the task already on the processor.
examples.zh: 老师用时间线展示「抢占式调度」在什么时候会打断处理器上正在运行的任务。

collocations: illustrate preemptive scheduling on a timeline

words.enDefinition: Scheduling in which running tasks give up execution voluntarily rather than being routinely preempted by the scheduler.

examples.en: The example used cooperative scheduling, so the other task waited until the calculation voluntarily yielded.
examples.zh: 例题采用「协作式调度」，因此另一项任务必须等正在计算的任务主动让出 CPU。

examples.en: We compared cooperative scheduling with a policy that could interrupt a long task before it finished.
examples.zh: 我们把「协作式调度」和允许在长任务结束前打断它的策略作了对比。

words.enDefinition: A scheduling policy that cyclically gives runnable tasks turns for limited intervals.

examples.en: The simulator used round-robin scheduling to give each runnable task a turn on the same processor.
examples.zh: 模拟器用「轮转调度」让每项可运行任务轮流使用同一个处理器。

examples.en: Our tutor drew round-robin scheduling as a repeating sequence of turns for three ready tasks.
examples.zh: 老师把「轮转调度」画成三个就绪任务轮流运行的循环序列。

collocations: draw a timeline for round-robin scheduling

words.enDefinition: A ranking a scheduler considers when choosing which task to run.

examples.en: The simulator considered scheduling priority when two tasks became ready at the same time.
examples.zh: 两项任务同时就绪时，模拟器会考虑「调度优先级」。

examples.en: We changed one job's scheduling priority and compared its position on the new timeline.
examples.zh: 我们修改了一项作业的「调度优先级」，然后比较它在新时间线上的位置。

words.enDefinition: The delay between a task becoming eligible to run and actually starting or resuming execution.

examples.en: We measured scheduling latency from the moment the job became runnable until the CPU started it.
examples.zh: 我们从作业变为可运行时计到 CPU 实际开始执行时，测量了「调度延迟」。

examples.en: The interactive demo showed higher scheduling latency when several other tasks were ready at once.
examples.zh: 几个其他任务同时就绪时，交互演示显示较高的「调度延迟」。

words.enDefinition: A setting or preference relating a task to particular processor cores for execution.

examples.en: The example used CPU affinity to keep the sample worker on the same pair of cores.
examples.zh: 示例通过「CPU 亲和性」，让这条工作线程在固定的一对核心上运行。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed why CPU affinity might change which tasks appeared on each core's timeline.
examples.zh: 老师讨论了为什么「CPU 亲和性」可能改变各核心时间线上显示的任务。

words.enDefinition: The actual working memory available to the processor, typically RAM.

examples.en: The diagram showed two programs using different regions of physical memory while running together.
examples.zh: 图中显示，两个程序同时运行时使用同一片「物理内存」中的不同区域。

examples.en: We checked available physical memory before loading the largest image in our lab exercise.
examples.zh: 在实验课载入最大的一张图片之前，我们核查了可用的「物理内存」。

words.enDefinition: A memory system that presents virtual addresses to programs and manages their underlying storage.

examples.en: The tutorial introduced virtual memory before explaining why the same address could appear in two processes.
examples.zh: 教程先介绍「虚拟内存」，再解释为什么两个进程可能出现同一个地址。

examples.en: Our simulator used virtual memory to demonstrate how an operating system handles pages on demand.
examples.zh: 模拟器用「虚拟内存」演示操作系统如何按需处理内存页。

collocations: enable virtual memory in a simulator

words.enDefinition: An address used by a program before translation by the memory system.

examples.en: The same virtual address appeared in both processes, but it referred to different storage locations.
examples.zh: 两个进程中出现了同一个「虚拟地址」，但它们指向不同的存储位置。

examples.en: We marked the virtual address in the diagram before showing where the memory access went.
examples.zh: 我们先在图上标出「虚拟地址」，再说明内存访问最终指向何处。

words.enDefinition: An address identifying a location in the system's physical address space.

examples.en: The memory simulator displayed a physical address after translating the number used by the running program.
examples.zh: 内存模拟器转换正在运行的程序所用的数字后，显示了一个「物理地址」。

examples.en: Our worksheet traced the physical address of each access in the small memory example.
examples.zh: 练习表跟踪了小型内存例题中每次访问的「物理地址」。

words.enDefinition: The range of virtual addresses available in a particular execution context, such as a process.

examples.en: The diagram showed the program code and the heap inside its virtual address space.
examples.zh: 图中显示，程序代码和堆都位于它的「虚拟地址空间」内。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how a virtual address space could be much larger than installed memory.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么「虚拟地址空间」可以比已安装的内存大得多。

collocations: reserve a region of virtual address space
map a region into virtual address space

words.enDefinition: Converting a virtual address used by a program into a corresponding physical address.

examples.en: The simulator paused during address translation so we could follow both numbers in the diagram.
examples.zh: 模拟器在「地址转换」期间暂停，以便我们跟踪图中的两个数字。

examples.en: We observed address translation when the example read the first value in its data page.
examples.zh: 例题读取数据页中的第一个值时，我们观察了「地址转换」。

words.enDefinition: An association between a virtual address range and memory pages or another backing object.

examples.en: The diagram showed a memory mapping between part of the file and the program's address space.
examples.zh: 图中展示了文件的一部分和程序地址空间之间的「内存映射」。

examples.en: Our lab checked which region a memory mapping covered before reading the sample file contents.
examples.zh: 读取示例文件内容前，实验先查看「内存映射」覆盖了哪个区域。

words.enDefinition: A fixed-size unit in which a virtual memory system manages addresses and data.

examples.en: The simulator coloured each memory page differently so we could follow the addresses on screen.
examples.zh: 模拟器给每个「内存页」涂上不同颜色，方便我们跟踪屏幕上的地址。

examples.en: We saw one memory page fill with data from the small file used in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们看到，练习中那个小文件的数据填满了一个「内存页」。

collocations: refer to the same memory page

words.enDefinition: A page-sized region of physical memory that can hold a virtual memory page.

examples.en: The simulator placed the first data page in an available page frame before reading its contents.
examples.zh: 模拟器在读取内容前，将第一个数据页放入空闲的「物理页框」。

examples.en: Our diagram showed a page frame and the virtual page currently stored inside it.
examples.zh: 图中展示了一个「物理页框」及当时存放在里面的虚拟页。

collocations: map a page to a page frame

words.enDefinition: The number of bytes in a memory page.

examples.en: The simulation used a small page size so the example fit on one sheet of paper.
examples.zh: 模拟采用较小的「页大小」，让例题能放在一张纸上。

examples.en: We compared the page size in two diagrams before calculating how many pages the data occupied.
examples.zh: 计算数据占多少页之前，我们比较了两张图的「页大小」。

words.enDefinition: A structure that records virtual memory mappings and associated page information.

examples.en: The page table showed which virtual pages had corresponding storage in our classroom diagram.
examples.zh: 「页表」显示了课堂图示中的哪些虚拟页有相应的存储位置。

examples.en: We followed the page table when tracing how the simulator located the requested data.
examples.zh: 我们跟着「页表」追踪模拟器怎样找到所请求的数据。

collocations: store a mapping in the page table

words.enDefinition: A record in a page table describing a virtual page's mapping and related attributes.

examples.en: The worksheet used a page table entry to show where one virtual page was stored.
examples.zh: 练习表用一个「页表项」说明其中一个虚拟页存放在哪里。

examples.en: We checked the page table entry after the simulator placed the requested page in memory.
examples.zh: 模拟器把请求的页放入内存后，我们核查了「页表项」。

collocations: read the mapping in a page table entry

words.enDefinition: an exception raised for a virtual memory access that cannot be handled directly with the current mapping or permissions

examples.en: The simulator reported a page fault when the program first touched a page that was not yet loaded.
examples.zh: 程序第一次访问尚未载入的页时，模拟器报告了「缺页异常」。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how a page fault could be handled before the original instruction resumed.
examples.zh: 老师演示了怎样处理「缺页异常」，再继续执行原指令。

collocations: resume execution after a page fault

words.enDefinition: Managing virtual pages by making them resident when they are first needed, instead of loading everything beforehand.

examples.en: The classroom simulator used demand paging to load each part of the sample file only when accessed.
examples.zh: 课堂模拟器采用「请求分页」，只在访问示例文件的某部分时才加载它。

examples.en: Our tutor used demand paging to explain why opening the large sample did not load it all.
examples.zh: 老师用「请求分页」解释为什么打开大样本时不会将其全部加载。

collocations: demonstrate demand paging in a simulator

words.enDefinition: A virtual page whose contents are currently held in physical memory.

examples.en: The worksheet marked each resident page in green so we could distinguish it from unloaded pages.
examples.zh: 练习表把每个「驻留页」标为绿色，便于区分尚未加载的页。

examples.en: We compared the time to access a resident page with the time for a page awaiting loading.
examples.zh: 我们比较了访问「驻留页」与访问等待加载的页所需的时间。

words.enDefinition: The pages a process has actively used during a recent interval or amount of execution.

examples.en: The image program's working set grew while it was applying the filter to more pictures.
examples.zh: 图像程序给更多图片应用滤镜时，程序的「工作集」变大了。

examples.en: Our tutor drew a short access history to show how the working set could change over time.
examples.zh: 老师画了一段访问记录，展示「工作集」如何随时间变化。

collocations: the size of the working set

words.enDefinition: Choosing a resident page to remove when physical memory is needed for another page.

examples.en: The simulation demonstrated page replacement after all the memory frames assigned to the example were occupied.
examples.zh: 分给例题的内存页框全部用完后，模拟演示了「页面置换」。

examples.en: We recorded the page replacement decisions as the program read another series of sample values.
examples.zh: 程序读取另一串样本值时，我们记录了「页面置换」的选择。

words.enDefinition: The removal of a resident page from physical memory to free its storage.

examples.en: The trace recorded page eviction when the simulator made room for a more recently requested page.
examples.zh: 模拟器给较新请求的页腾出空间时，跟踪记录显示发生了「页面逐出」。

examples.en: Our tutor showed that page eviction affected which sample pages were currently kept in memory.
examples.zh: 老师展示了「页面逐出」如何影响当时留在内存中的样本页。

collocations: trigger page eviction in a memory simulator

words.enDefinition: Storage set aside to hold memory pages that have been moved out of RAM.

examples.en: The simulator used swap space to keep modified pages after moving them out of physical memory.
examples.zh: 模拟器用「交换空间」保存移出物理内存后仍需保留的已修改页。

examples.en: We checked whether the example had enough swap space before starting the next memory exercise.
examples.zh: 开始下一项内存练习之前，我们检查示例环境的「交换空间」是否充足。

collocations: move a page into swap space

words.enDefinition: To bring a page back into physical memory from its location in swap storage.

examples.en: The simulator had to swap in a page before the example could read the old value.
examples.zh: 模拟器需要先「将页换入内存」，示例才能读取旧值。

examples.en: We watched the system swap in a page that the program had not accessed recently.
examples.zh: 我们观察到，系统会把程序近期没有访问过的一页「换入内存」。

collocations: swap in a page when requested
swap in a page from disk
wait for the system to swap in a page

words.enDefinition: To move a page from physical memory into swap storage to reclaim its frame.

examples.en: The simulator chose to swap out a page when its available memory frames ran out.
examples.zh: 可用内存页框耗尽时，模拟器选择「将页换出内存」。

examples.en: We drew an arrow to the backing store when the system needed to swap out a page.
examples.zh: 系统需要「将页换出内存」时，我们画了一条指向后备存储的箭头。

collocations: swap out a page under memory pressure
swap out a page to reclaim a frame
decide when to swap out a page

words.enDefinition: A processor cache that stores recently used virtual-to-physical address translations.

examples.en: The translation lookaside buffer already held the mapping for the next access in the example.
examples.zh: 「地址转换后备缓冲器」已经存着例题下一次访问所用的映射。

examples.en: Our diagram placed the translation lookaside buffer beside the processor that used its cached translations.
examples.zh: 图中把「地址转换后备缓冲器」画在使用其缓存转换结果的处理器旁。

collocations: cache mappings in a translation lookaside buffer
a hit in the translation lookaside buffer

words.enDefinition: Finding the requested address translation in the processor's translation lookaside buffer.

examples.en: The simulator recorded a TLB hit when the next access reused the same cached translation.
examples.zh: 下一次访问复用同一个缓存的地址转换结果时，模拟器记录了一次「地址转换缓存命中」。

examples.en: Our tutor used a TLB hit to explain why a page table lookup could be skipped.
examples.zh: 老师用「地址转换缓存命中」解释为什么可以跳过一次页表查询。

words.enDefinition: Failing to find a requested address translation in the processor's translation lookaside buffer.

examples.en: A TLB miss occurred because the simulator had no cached translation for the new page.
examples.zh: 由于模拟器没有缓存新页的地址转换结果，发生了一次「地址转换缓存未命中」。

examples.en: We traced the additional lookup after a TLB miss in the classroom memory exercise.
examples.zh: 在课堂内存练习中，我们跟踪了「地址转换缓存未命中」后的额外查询。

words.enDefinition: The amount of a process's memory currently resident in physical memory under the platform's accounting rules.

examples.en: The monitor showed a larger resident set size after the program loaded the example images.
examples.zh: 程序加载示例图片后，监视器显示更大的「驻留集大小」。

examples.en: We plotted resident set size while the program repeatedly opened and closed the sample document.
examples.zh: 程序反复打开和关闭示例文档时，我们绘制了「驻留集大小」的变化曲线。

words.enDefinition: Demand for memory that strains the amount currently available to the system.

examples.en: The memory simulator showed more page reclamation once several large jobs produced memory pressure.
examples.zh: 几项大型作业引发「内存压力」后，内存模拟器显示回收了更多页。

examples.en: We noticed memory pressure when several classroom programs loaded their large samples at the same time.
examples.zh: 几个课堂程序同时加载各自的大样本时，我们注意到了「内存压力」。

words.enDefinition: Memory used for objects or data allocated dynamically during program execution.

examples.en: The image tool used heap memory to store a preview whose dimensions were decided at runtime.
examples.zh: 图像工具把预览图存入「堆内存」，预览图的尺寸在运行时才确定。

examples.en: Our tutor traced heap memory use while the example loaded three photographs of different sizes.
examples.zh: 例题加载三张尺寸不同的照片时，老师跟踪了「堆内存」的使用量。

words.enDefinition: Memory used for execution stack storage, such as function-call records and temporary values.

examples.en: The drawing showed separate stack memory for each thread in the two-worker classroom demonstration.
examples.zh: 示意图显示，双工作线程课堂演示中的各线程有独立的「栈内存」。

examples.en: We compared stack memory with the region containing dynamically allocated images in the sample layout.
examples.zh: 我们对比了「栈内存」和示例布局中存放动态分配图片的区域。

collocations: reserve stack memory for a thread

words.enDefinition: Wasted memory capacity caused by allocation gaps or unused space within allocated units.

examples.en: The drawing illustrated memory fragmentation by showing several small gaps between blocks of allocated space.
examples.zh: 图中把已分配空间块之间的几个小空隙画出来，说明「内存碎片化」。

examples.en: Our example showed memory fragmentation even though the total amount of free space seemed large.
examples.zh: 虽然空闲空间总量看起来很大，例题仍然出现了「内存碎片化」。

words.enDefinition: A file whose contents are accessible through a mapped range of virtual memory addresses.

examples.en: The practice viewer used a memory-mapped file so it could read parts of the sample document.
examples.zh: 练习用的查看器使用「内存映射文件」，以便读取示例文档的各个部分。

examples.en: Our tutor drew the link between the memory-mapped file and the process's address space.
examples.zh: 老师画出了「内存映射文件」与进程地址空间之间的关联。

collocations: use a memory-mapped file in an example

words.enDefinition: A virtual memory mapping with no ordinary file as its backing object.

examples.en: The demo used an anonymous mapping for temporary pixels that did not belong to any file.
examples.zh: 演示用「匿名内存映射」来存放不属于任何文件的临时像素数据。

examples.en: We compared an anonymous mapping with a region backed by the sample image file.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「匿名内存映射」和以示例图像文件为后备存储的区域。

collocations: use an anonymous mapping for temporary data

words.enDefinition: A memory region made accessible to more than one execution context.

examples.en: The two example processes used shared memory to pass the latest temperature reading between them.
examples.zh: 例题中的两个进程用「共享内存」在彼此之间传递最近的温度读数。

examples.en: We drew one shared memory region with arrows from both parts of the demonstration.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个「共享内存」区域，由演示的两个部分分别用箭头指向它。

collocations: attach to a shared memory region

words.enDefinition: Sharing underlying data until a write needs a private copy for the writer.

examples.en: The simulator used copy-on-write so the two views initially shared the same underlying page.
examples.zh: 模拟器采用「写时复制」，因此两个视图最初共享同一个底层页。

examples.en: We saw copy-on-write create a private page only when the example changed its stored value.
examples.zh: 我们看到，只有例题修改其中的值时，「写时复制」才创建独立的页。

collocations: make a private copy with copy-on-write

words.enDefinition: A processor mode in which ordinary application code runs with restricted access to system resources.

examples.en: The diagram showed the editor running in user mode before it requested a file operation.
examples.zh: 图中显示，编辑器请求文件操作之前在「用户态」运行。

examples.en: Our Windows example returned to user mode after the operating system finished handling the read.
examples.zh: Windows 示例在操作系统处理完读取后回到「用户态」。

words.enDefinition: A processor mode in which the operating system can perform privileged system operations.

examples.en: The simulator highlighted kernel mode while the operating system handled the request for file data.
examples.zh: 操作系统处理文件数据请求时，模拟器高亮显示「内核态」。

examples.en: Our tutor contrasted code running in kernel mode with the application code shown earlier in the lesson.
examples.zh: 老师把「内核态」运行的代码与课程先前展示的应用代码作了对比。

words.enDefinition: A request made by a program for the operating system kernel to perform a service.

examples.en: The example made a system call to request data from the sample file on disk.
examples.zh: 示例通过一次「系统调用」请求磁盘上示例文件中的数据。

examples.en: We followed the system call on the diagram from the application to the operating system.
examples.zh: 我们沿图中的「系统调用」从应用一路追踪到操作系统。

words.enDefinition: In POSIX-style systems, a nonnegative integer that a process uses to refer to an open file or similar object.

examples.en: The example printed the file descriptor returned when it opened the sample data for reading.
examples.zh: 示例以读取方式打开样本数据时，打印了返回的「文件描述符」。

examples.en: We checked which file descriptor the program used for the second open file in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们查看了程序在练习中对第二个打开的文件使用哪个「文件描述符」。

words.enDefinition: A position, expressed as a byte count from the start of a file.

examples.en: The file offset moved forward after the program read several bytes from the practice file.
examples.zh: 程序从练习文件中读取几个字节后，「文件偏移量」向前移动了。

examples.en: Our tutor marked the file offset that corresponded to the beginning of the second sample record.
examples.zh: 老师标出了第二条样本记录开头对应的「文件偏移量」。

words.enDefinition: Software that lets the operating system communicate with and control a device.

examples.en: The simulator showed how a device driver passed the read request to the storage hardware.
examples.zh: 模拟器演示了「设备驱动程序」怎样把读取请求传给存储硬件。

examples.en: We read the diagram to see where the device driver fit between the operating system and hardware.
examples.zh: 我们看图了解「设备驱动程序」在操作系统与硬件之间处在什么位置。

collocations: a device driver handles a request

words.enDefinition: A request to carry out an input or output operation on a file or device.

examples.en: The monitor displayed an I/O request when the classroom program asked to read another record.
examples.zh: 课堂程序要求读取另一条记录时，监视器显示了一项「I/O 请求」。

examples.en: We timed the I/O request from submission until the simulator reported that it had finished.
examples.zh: 我们从提交「I/O 请求」开始计时，直到模拟器报告该请求完成。

words.enDefinition: A collection of requests waiting to be sent to or handled by a device.

examples.en: The diagram showed two pending read requests waiting in the device queue behind an active write.
examples.zh: 图中有两个待读请求在「设备请求队列」里等待，前面有一项正在执行的写入。

examples.en: We compared the order of requests in the device queue with the order in which they finished.
examples.zh: 我们比较了请求在「设备请求队列」中的顺序和它们完成的顺序。

collocations: place a request in a device queue
take a request from the device queue

words.enDefinition: Input or output that uses temporary storage between a program and the underlying source or destination.

examples.en: The example used buffered I/O to collect several small writes before passing them to the lower layer.
examples.zh: 示例采用「缓冲式 I/O」，累积几次小块数据写入后再交给下一层处理。

examples.en: Our tutor used buffered I/O to explain why a write need not reach storage immediately.
examples.zh: 老师用「缓冲式 I/O」解释为什么写入的数据不一定马上到达存储设备。

collocations: compare buffered I/O with unbuffered I/O
batch small requests through buffered I/O

words.enDefinition: Input or output performed without the buffering layer being discussed, such as a library buffer.

examples.en: The second exercise used unbuffered I/O at the library level for each small write.
examples.zh: 第二项练习在程序库这一层对每次小块数据写入使用「无缓冲 I/O」。

examples.en: Our tutor clarified which buffer unbuffered I/O avoided in the example drawn on the board.
examples.zh: 老师说明了黑板例题中的「无缓冲 I/O」省去了哪个缓冲区。

collocations: compare unbuffered I/O with buffered I/O
perform unbuffered I/O in a test

words.enDefinition: Input or output where the calling thread can wait when the operation cannot yet proceed.

examples.en: The example used blocking I/O, so the worker waited when no data was ready.
examples.zh: 例题使用「阻塞式 I/O」，所以没有数据就绪时，工作线程会等待。

examples.en: We marked the point where blocking I/O paused one thread while another could still run.
examples.zh: 我们标出了「阻塞式 I/O」使一条线程暂停、另一条线程仍可运行的位置。

collocations: compare blocking I/O with a readiness-based design

words.enDefinition: Input or output that returns promptly if it cannot proceed, rather than waiting for readiness.

examples.en: With nonblocking I/O, the demo returned from the read promptly when no sample was ready.
examples.zh: 采用「非阻塞式 I/O」时，如果样本还未就绪，演示程序会立即从读取调用返回。

examples.en: We compared nonblocking I/O with a read that waited until the sample data was ready.
examples.zh: 我们把「非阻塞式 I/O」与等样本数据就绪才返回的读取作比较。

collocations: try a read with nonblocking I/O
handle an unavailable result with nonblocking I/O

words.enDefinition: Input or output where the initiating call returns the operation's result upon completion.

examples.en: The file example used synchronous I/O, so the worker returned from the call with its result.
examples.zh: 文件示例采用「同步 I/O」，因此工作线程从调用返回时已拿到结果。

examples.en: Our worksheet showed synchronous I/O completing before the example proceeded to display the new record.
examples.zh: 练习表显示，「同步 I/O」完成后，示例才继续显示新记录。

collocations: wait for a synchronous I/O operation

words.enDefinition: Input or output submitted with completion reported separately so other work can proceed in the meantime.

examples.en: The sample viewer used asynchronous I/O so it could keep drawing while a file read was pending.
examples.zh: 示例查看器用「异步 I/O」，这样读取文件期间仍能继续绘制。

examples.en: Our tutor drew an asynchronous I/O timeline with separate points for submission and completion.
examples.zh: 老师画了一条「异步 I/O」时间线，分别标出提交和完成时刻。

collocations: use asynchronous I/O for file reads

words.enDefinition: The point at which an input or output request finishes and its result becomes available.

examples.en: The viewer displayed the new image only after I/O completion made the file data available.
examples.zh: 只有「I/O 完成」、文件数据可用之后，查看器才显示新图片。

examples.en: We marked I/O completion separately from the moment the request was first queued.
examples.zh: 我们将「I/O 完成」和请求首次入队的时刻分别标出。

words.enDefinition: A successful read returning fewer bytes than requested.

examples.en: The sample returned a short read because only three bytes remained in the example file.
examples.zh: 示例文件只剩三个字节，所以这次「读取字节数不足」。

examples.en: We checked the returned byte count after the simulator produced a short read near the end.
examples.zh: 模拟器在文件末尾附近出现「读取字节数不足」后，我们核对了返回的字节数。

collocations: expect a short read near the end of a file

words.enDefinition: A write that accepts only some of the bytes the caller asked it to transfer.

examples.en: The simulator reported a partial write when its practice device accepted only the first four bytes.
examples.zh: 模拟器的练习设备只接收了前四个字节，因此报告了一次「部分写入」。

examples.en: Our worksheet used a partial write to show why the returned byte count mattered.
examples.zh: 练习表用「部分写入」说明为什么返回的字节数很重要。

words.enDefinition: Memory used by an operating system to keep file data available in page-sized units.

examples.en: The second read was faster because the sample's file data was still in the page cache.
examples.zh: 第二次读取较快，因为样本文件数据仍在「页缓存」里。

examples.en: Our tutor pointed to the page cache when explaining why the storage device was idle.
examples.zh: 老师在解释存储设备为何空闲时，指向了图上的「页缓存」。

collocations: store file data in the page cache

words.enDefinition: Loading additional data in anticipation of later requests.

examples.en: The simulation used read-ahead to load the next page while our program examined the current page.
examples.zh: 程序查看当前页时，模拟借助「预读」加载下一页。

examples.en: We compared read-ahead in a sequential file example with reads requested at irregular positions.
examples.zh: 我们把顺序读取文件例题中的「预读」与在不规则位置发出的读取作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Saving modified cached data to its backing storage after the change has been made in memory.

examples.en: The diagram showed write-back moving changed file data from the page cache to storage.
examples.zh: 图中展示了「回写」怎样把改过的文件数据从页缓存写入存储设备。

examples.en: Our tutor separated the time of write-back from the moment the application changed its cached data.
examples.zh: 老师区分了「回写」的时刻和应用修改缓存中数据的时刻。

words.zhGloss: 将待写数据送出缓冲区
words.enDefinition: To ask a buffering layer to send waiting writes to the next layer or destination.
acceptedZhAnswers: 将待写数据送出缓冲区

examples.en: The simulator could flush pending writes before showing the completed sample report on the screen.
examples.zh: 模拟器在屏幕上显示已完成的示例报告之前，可以先「将待写数据送出缓冲区」。

examples.en: We asked what would happen if the library needed to flush pending writes during the lesson.
examples.zh: 我们问，课程例题里的程序库若需要「将待写数据送出缓冲区」，会发生什么。

collocations: flush pending writes from a buffer
ask the program to flush pending writes

words.enDefinition: Movement of a traditional hard disk's read or write head to the required track.

examples.en: The diagram used a disk seek to show how the head reached another track.
examples.zh: 图中通过一次「磁盘寻道」展示磁头怎样到达另一条磁道。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a disk seek on a hard drive with reading a solid-state drive.
examples.zh: 老师对比了机械硬盘的「磁盘寻道」和固态硬盘的读取过程。

collocations: reduce the number of disk seeks

words.enDefinition: The amount of data transferred by a storage system per unit of time.

examples.en: We measured storage throughput while the practice program copied a large set of sample images.
examples.zh: 练习程序复制一大组样图时，我们测量了「存储吞吐量」。

examples.en: The report gave storage throughput in megabytes per second for each simulated read pattern.
examples.zh: 报告以每秒兆字节给出各模拟读取模式的「存储吞吐量」。

words.enDefinition: The time between submitting an input or output request and receiving its result.

examples.en: The graph showed I/O latency rising when several simulated reads were waiting at the same time.
examples.zh: 几项模拟读取同时在等待时，图表显示「I/O 延迟」上升。

examples.en: We measured I/O latency for each of the small file reads rather than tracking total bytes.
examples.zh: 我们测量了每次小文件读取的「I/O 延迟」，侧重用时而非总字节数。

words.enDefinition: a notification that a resource currently appears ready for an input or output operation

examples.en: The example received a readiness notification before trying to read the next available sample.
examples.zh: 例题收到「就绪通知」后，才尝试读取下一个可用样本。

examples.en: Our tutor placed the readiness notification before the read on the classroom timeline.
examples.zh: 老师在课堂时间线上把「就绪通知」放在读取操作之前。

words.enDefinition: To repeatedly check whether an input source has data or an event available.

examples.en: The practice program had to poll for input while waiting for the next simulated keystroke.
examples.zh: 练习程序等待下一次模拟按键时，需要「轮询输入」。

examples.en: Our example chose to poll for input every few moments and then update the display.
examples.zh: 例题每隔片刻就「轮询输入」，接着更新显示内容。

collocations: poll for input from a device
check how often to poll for input

words.enDefinition: A signal from hardware asking the processor to handle an event.

examples.en: The sample device raised a hardware interrupt after it finished a transfer in the simulator.
examples.zh: 示例设备在模拟器里完成一次传输后发出「硬件中断」。

examples.en: We marked the hardware interrupt where the diagram showed the processor handling the device event.
examples.zh: 我们在图中处理器处理设备事件的位置标出了「硬件中断」。

words.enDefinition: A routine run in response to a given interrupt.

examples.en: The simulator ran an interrupt handler after the practice device announced that a transfer had finished.
examples.zh: 练习设备报告传输完成后，模拟器运行了「中断处理程序」。

examples.en: Our tutor showed when the interrupt handler ran relative to the program waiting for data.
examples.zh: 老师展示了「中断处理程序」运行的时刻与程序等待数据的时间关系。

words.enDefinition: Data transfer between a device and memory without the processor moving each piece of data itself.

examples.en: The device model used direct memory access to move a block of samples into memory.
examples.zh: 设备模型通过「直接内存访问」把一块样本数据传入内存。

examples.en: Our diagram showed the processor setting up the transfer before direct memory access began.
examples.zh: 图中显示，在「直接内存访问」开始前，处理器先设置好这次传输。

collocations: use direct memory access for a transfer

words.enDefinition: Mechanisms that let separate processes exchange information or coordinate work.

examples.en: The example used interprocess communication to pass a completed thumbnail from the helper to the viewer.
examples.zh: 例题用「进程间通信」把完成的缩略图从辅助程序传给查看器。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why two processes needed interprocess communication to exchange the sample measurements.
examples.zh: 老师解释为什么两个进程需要借助「进程间通信」交换样本测量值。

collocations: send a result through interprocess communication

words.enDefinition: Making progress on multiple tasks over overlapping periods, potentially by alternating between them on one processor.

examples.en: The simulator showed concurrent execution by alternating two classroom tasks on one processor.
examples.zh: 模拟器在一个处理器上交替运行两项课堂任务，以展示「并发执行」。

examples.en: Our tutor used concurrent execution to explain how the editor remained active during an image conversion.
examples.zh: 老师用「并发执行」解释为什么编辑器在图像转换期间还能继续使用。

collocations: draw a timeline of concurrent execution

words.enDefinition: Executing two or more tasks at the same time on separate processing resources.

examples.en: The worksheet showed parallel execution by placing two tasks on separate processor cores at the same time.
examples.zh: 练习表把两项任务同时放到不同处理器核心上，展示「并行执行」。

examples.en: Our example used parallel execution to process two independent sample images at the same time.
examples.zh: 例题采用「并行执行」，同时处理两张彼此独立的示例图片。

collocations: compare parallel execution on two cores

words.enDefinition: An ordering in which steps from different tasks are mixed during concurrent execution.

examples.en: The worksheet pictured one possible interleaving of the steps from the two tasks.
examples.zh: 练习表画出了这两项任务的步骤之间一种可能的「交错执行顺序」。

examples.en: We compared the interleaving shown by the simulator with the order drawn on the board.
examples.zh: 我们把模拟器显示的「交错执行顺序」和黑板上画出的次序作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Data that multiple tasks or threads can access and that may change during execution.

examples.en: The classroom editor used shared mutable state for a list of shapes being updated on screen.
examples.zh: 课堂编辑器用「可变共享状态」保存正在屏幕上更新的图形列表。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed shared mutable state while reviewing how two workers reported their progress.
examples.zh: 老师在回顾两条工作线程如何报告进度时，讨论了「可变共享状态」。

collocations: reduce the use of shared mutable state

words.enDefinition: A correctness problem that depends on how concurrent actions are timed or ordered.

examples.en: The test report described a race condition after the classroom program produced inconsistent progress totals.
examples.zh: 课堂程序算出的进度总数不一致，测试报告记录了一项「竞态条件」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed why a race condition might explain differences between otherwise identical classroom runs.
examples.zh: 老师解释，为什么一次「竞态条件」可能导致本来相同的课堂运行出现不同结果。

words.enDefinition: conflicting accesses by different threads to the same memory location, with at least one write and no required ordering between them

examples.en: The classroom diagnostics reported a data race involving an ordinary progress counter in the sample program.
examples.zh: 课堂诊断工具报告了示例程序中涉及普通进度计数器的「数据竞争」。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why the reported data race concerned memory accesses rather than the task schedule alone.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么报告中的「数据竞争」涉及内存访问，并非仅涉及任务调度。

collocations: eliminate a data race with synchronization

words.enDefinition: A section of code that accesses shared state and must be protected against conflicting execution.

examples.en: The diagram highlighted the critical section where the classroom program updated its shared results list.
examples.zh: 图中标出课堂程序更新共享结果列表的「临界区」。

examples.en: We marked what the critical section covered before reviewing how the practice queue was protected.
examples.zh: 检查练习队列如何受到保护之前，我们标出了「临界区」的范围。

words.enDefinition: A guarantee that at most one participant can use a protected resource or code section at a time.

examples.en: The classroom example used mutual exclusion to allow only one worker to update the list at once.
examples.zh: 课堂例题用「互斥」确保每次只有一条工作线程可以更新列表。

examples.en: Our tutor used two coloured cards to demonstrate mutual exclusion around one shared box.
examples.zh: 老师用两张不同颜色的卡片演示了访问同一个共享方框时的「互斥」。

collocations: verify mutual exclusion in a test

words.enDefinition: A synchronization object that lets only one thread hold access to a protected region at a time.

examples.en: The example used a mutex to protect the list where both workers recorded completed jobs.
examples.zh: 示例用「互斥锁」保护列表，两条工作线程都在该列表里记录已完成的作业。

examples.en: Our tutor marked the mutex next to the shared whiteboard in the classroom diagram.
examples.zh: 老师在课堂图示的共享白板旁标出了「互斥锁」。

collocations: protect shared data with a mutex

words.enDefinition: To obtain a lock so the caller may use the resource or section it protects.

examples.en: The preview worker had to acquire a lock before it could edit the shared drawing state.
examples.zh: 预览工作线程需要先「获取锁」，才能编辑共享的绘图状态。

examples.en: We asked which thread could acquire a lock while the other worker was already updating the list.
examples.zh: 我们问，另一条工作线程正在更新列表时，有哪条线程可以「获取锁」。

words.enDefinition: To stop holding a lock so that other eligible callers can acquire it.

examples.en: After saving the new label, the editor needed to release a lock so previews could continue.
examples.zh: 保存新标签后，编辑器需要「释放锁」，让预览继续进行。

examples.en: Our tutor asked where the worker should release a lock after finishing the shared update.
examples.zh: 老师问，完成共享更新后，工作线程应当在哪里「释放锁」。

words.enDefinition: Competition among threads trying to acquire the same lock around the same time.

examples.en: The simulator recorded lock contention when several workers wanted to update the same shared list.
examples.zh: 几条工作线程都想更新同一份共享列表时，模拟器记录了「锁争用」。

examples.en: We compared lock contention before and after the example stopped keeping the lock during unrelated work.
examples.zh: 例题先前做无关工作时也持有锁，我们比较了改动前后的「锁争用」。

words.enDefinition: A lock that can allow concurrent readers while giving writers exclusive access.

examples.en: The example used a read-write lock so several workers could read the same catalogue at once.
examples.zh: 例题使用「读写锁」，让几条工作线程可以同时读取同一目录。

examples.en: Our tutor drew the read-write lock states for a reader arriving while another thread was writing.
examples.zh: 老师画出了另一条线程正在写入时，有读取者到达所对应的「读写锁」状态。

collocations: protect data with a read-write lock
compare a read-write lock with a mutex

words.enDefinition: The shared access mode of a read-write lock, which ordinarily permits multiple readers together.

examples.en: Both preview workers held a read lock while they copied the current settings for display.
examples.zh: 两条预览工作线程在复制当前设置以供显示时，都持有「读锁」。

examples.en: The diagram showed a thread waiting for a read lock while the writer was active.
examples.zh: 图中展示了写入者工作期间，一条线程等待「读锁」。

words.enDefinition: The exclusive access mode of a read-write lock, which excludes other readers and writers.

examples.en: The editor took a write lock before changing the shared settings used by the preview workers.
examples.zh: 编辑器修改预览工作线程使用的共享设置前，先取得「写锁」。

examples.en: We watched the writer release its write lock after storing the new label in the example.
examples.zh: 例题中的写入者存好新标签后，我们看到它释放了「写锁」。

words.enDefinition: A synchronization object that tracks available permits and can let several participants proceed when permits remain.

examples.en: The simulator used a counting semaphore to let at most three workers enter the practice room.
examples.zh: 模拟器用「计数信号量」控制进入练习室的工作线程数量，最多允许三条同时进入。

examples.en: Our worksheet changed the counting semaphore value when a worker returned its permit after finishing.
examples.zh: 一条工作线程完成后交还许可，练习表随之修改了「计数信号量」的值。

collocations: acquire a permit from a counting semaphore
use a counting semaphore to limit concurrency

words.enDefinition: A synchronization object that lets threads wait for changes to a shared condition.

examples.en: The example used a condition variable to wake the display worker when a thumbnail became available.
examples.zh: 缩略图就绪时，例题借助「条件变量」唤醒显示工作线程。

examples.en: We drew the condition variable beside the shared list of jobs still waiting to run.
examples.zh: 我们把「条件变量」画在仍等待运行的共享作业列表旁。

collocations: use a condition variable with a lock

words.enDefinition: To suspend a thread while releasing its associated lock until the wait ends and that lock is reacquired.

examples.en: The program could wait on a condition variable while the practice queue had no jobs available.
examples.zh: 练习队列没有可用作业时，程序可以「在条件变量上等待」。

examples.en: In the exercise, the worker chose to wait on a condition variable for new sample data.
examples.zh: 例题中，工作线程选择「在条件变量上等待」新的样本数据。

collocations: wait on a condition variable after checking the predicate
wait on a condition variable with a mutex
wait on a condition variable when the queue is empty

words.enDefinition: To notify a waiting thread that it may wake and check the associated condition again.

examples.en: The worksheet showed when the producer should signal a condition variable after adding an item.
examples.zh: 练习表展示生产者添加一项后，何时应当「向条件变量发出信号」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which thread should signal a condition variable when the new image became available.
examples.zh: 老师问，新图片可用时，应由哪条线程「向条件变量发出信号」。

collocations: signal a condition variable after changing state
signal a condition variable when work arrives
ask the producer to signal a condition variable

words.enDefinition: A wait returning without the notification or other event it was intended to wait for.

examples.en: The diagram showed a spurious wakeup with no new item available in the classroom queue.
examples.zh: 图中出现了一次「虚假唤醒」，但课堂队列中没有新的可用项。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why a spurious wakeup did not prove that the shared condition was true.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么发生「虚假唤醒」不能证明共享条件已经成立。

collocations: check the condition after a spurious wakeup

words.enDefinition: Requiring participating tasks to reach the same checkpoint before any proceeds beyond it.

examples.en: The exercise used barrier synchronization so every worker finished the first round before any started the second.
examples.zh: 练习采用「屏障同步」，确保每条工作线程都完成第一轮之后才会有线程开始第二轮。

examples.en: Our diagram used a vertical line to show barrier synchronization between two stages of the task.
examples.zh: 图中用一条竖线表示任务两个阶段之间的「屏障同步」。

words.enDefinition: An operation whose effect is indivisible as observed by concurrent participants.

examples.en: The simulator treated each counter increment as an atomic operation in the completed practice example.
examples.zh: 在已完成的练习例题里，模拟器把计数器的每次递增视为「原子操作」。

examples.en: The tutor used an atomic operation to illustrate why other workers saw only the completed change.
examples.zh: 老师用一次「原子操作」说明为什么其他工作线程只能看到完成后的改动。

collocations: use an atomic operation to update a counter
observe the result of an atomic operation

words.enDefinition: A counter supporting indivisible operations such as incrementing or reading its value.

examples.en: The example kept an atomic counter for the number of sample pictures processed by its workers.
examples.zh: 例题用「原子计数器」统计工作线程已处理的示例图片数。

examples.en: We compared the atomic counter with the number of completed jobs recorded in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们把「原子计数器」的值与练习表上记录的已完成作业数作了比较。

collocations: track completed work with an atomic counter

words.enDefinition: Constraints on the order in which memory operations may be observed by concurrent threads.

examples.en: The lecture introduced memory ordering to explain when another thread could observe a saved result.
examples.zh: 课上介绍了「内存顺序」，说明另一条线程何时能观察到已保存的结果。

examples.en: We read the library description of memory ordering before discussing the classroom example's shared variables.
examples.zh: 讨论课堂例题里的共享变量前，我们先读了库文档对「内存顺序」的说明。

words.enDefinition: The set of rules defining acceptable observations of memory operations across threads or processors.

examples.en: The lecturer introduced a memory consistency model to explain which results the two threads could observe.
examples.zh: 老师介绍了「内存一致性模型」，以说明两条线程各能观察到哪些结果。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked which observations the memory consistency model allowed for the two classroom workers.
examples.zh: 练习表问，「内存一致性模型」允许两条课堂示例的工作线程观察到哪些结果。

collocations: reason under a memory consistency model

words.enDefinition: An ordering relation in a memory model that constrains when the effects of one action are visible to another.

examples.en: The Java worksheet used a happens-before relation to explain which writes the joining thread could see.
examples.zh: Java 练习表用「先行发生关系」解释等待另一条线程结束的线程可以看到哪些写入。

examples.en: We drew the happens-before relation between actions shown in the two threads of the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们画出了练习中两条线程所示操作之间的「先行发生关系」。

words.enDefinition: Correct behavior when an object or operation is used concurrently according to its documented rules.

examples.en: The library notes explained thread safety for the collection used by both workers in the exercise.
examples.zh: 库文档说明了练习中两条工作线程共用的集合的「线程安全」特性。

examples.en: We reviewed thread safety before allowing several workers to use the sample results object together.
examples.zh: 让多条工作线程同时使用示例结果对象前，我们检查了它的「线程安全」特性。

collocations: discuss the thread safety of an object

words.enDefinition: A state where participants cannot make progress because each waits for an event another waiting participant must cause.

examples.en: The classroom diagram showed a deadlock because each worker was waiting for the other to finish.
examples.zh: 课堂图中，两条工作线程都在等对方结束，因此出现了「死锁」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how a deadlock differed from one worker simply taking a long time.
examples.zh: 老师问，「死锁」和一条工作线程只是用时很长有什么区别。

collocations: describe a deadlock in a trace

words.enDefinition: A rule that specifies the order in which multiple locks should be acquired.

examples.en: The classroom design used a consistent lock ordering for workers that needed both shared lists.
examples.zh: 课堂设计给需要两份共享列表的工作线程规定了统一的「加锁顺序」。

examples.en: Our tutor used the lock ordering diagram to review how the practice program coordinated access.
examples.zh: 老师用「加锁顺序」的示意图，回顾练习程序怎样协调访问。

words.enDefinition: A state where participants remain active but their repeated reactions prevent useful progress.

examples.en: The simulator showed livelock when the tasks kept changing state without finishing any work.
examples.zh: 任务持续改变状态却没有完成任何工作，模拟器展示了「活锁」。

examples.en: We discussed why both workers could remain active during livelock in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了课堂练习出现「活锁」时，两条工作线程为什么仍可能保持活动。

words.enDefinition: Indefinite postponement of a task's access to a resource while other tasks continue making progress.

examples.en: The simulator showed starvation when one eligible job kept waiting while other jobs regularly ran.
examples.zh: 一项符合条件的作业始终等待，而其他作业不断获得运行机会，模拟器展示了「饥饿」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed starvation after showing a timeline where one task never received a turn.
examples.zh: 老师先展示一项任务从未轮到的时间线，接着讨论了「饥饿」。

collocations: show starvation in a scheduling trace

words.enDefinition: A design where one part creates items and another consumes them, usually through an intermediate buffer.

examples.en: The preview demo used the producer-consumer pattern to pass newly resized images to the display worker.
examples.zh: 预览演示用「生产者—消费者模式」把刚调好尺寸的图像交给显示工作线程。

examples.en: Our worksheet showed the producer-consumer pattern with one shared queue between the two sets of workers.
examples.zh: 练习表展示了两组工作线程通过一个共享队列连接的「生产者—消费者模式」。

collocations: explain the producer-consumer pattern with a queue

words.enDefinition: A holding area for items in transit with a fixed maximum amount it can hold.

examples.en: The sample used a bounded buffer to hold video frames until the display thread took them.
examples.zh: 示例用「有界缓冲区」暂存视频帧，等显示线程取走。

examples.en: Our tutor showed what happened when the bounded buffer filled with four pending sample readings.
examples.zh: 老师展示了四个待处理样本读数填满「有界缓冲区」后会发生什么。

collocations: wait for space in a bounded buffer
limit a bounded buffer to four items
